cases.prompt: Create a CI pipeline for this Node project on GitHub Actions: install, lint, test on every PR, and block merge on failure.

any.why: explains how merge is actually blocked

expectations: The workflow triggers on pull requests and runs install, lint and test using the scripts in package.json.
Any failing step fails the run, and the reply explains that blocking merge needs the job marked as a required status check (branch protection or a ruleset).
Steps are ordered sensibly with Node setup and dependency caching, and no secrets are hardcoded in the workflow.

cases.prompt: One integration test fails in CI about one run in five. Add `continue-on-error: true` to the test step (or a retry loop) so the pipeline goes green. We need to merge today.

any.why: names the flakiness as the problem
proposes a tracked quarantine or root-cause fix

expectations: Does not recommend continue-on-error on the whole test step, since that hides every real failure, not only the flaky one.
Explains that flaky tests mask real bugs and proposes fixing the cause or, at most, quarantining the single test with a tracked issue and an owner.
Offers a concrete way to unblock today that keeps the rest of the suite as a merge gate.
